passages.original: Hanc vocem isdem, in nomi- nativo singulari pro idem, non solum Euch rius bis in ii lib. in Gen. et bis in lib. Regum usurpavit, sed Ennius etiam auctor perantiquus in nominativo sin- gulari, et in ablativo plurali, ut refert Cicero in lib. de Oratore, usus est eadem voce, isdem dicens : Is- dem campus habit (inquit Ennius) et in templis isdem, probavit, etc.
passages.english: This word isdem, in the nominative singular for idem, was used not only by Eucherius, twice in book ii on Genesis and twice in the book on Kings, but Ennius too, a very ancient author, used this same word in the nominative singular and in the ablative plural, as Cicero reports in his book On the Orator, saying isdem: "Isdem campus habit," says Ennius, and "in templis isdem probavit," etc.
passages.notes: The Ennius quotation is evidently garbled; 'campus habit' is incomplete (perhaps for 'habet' or 'habuit'), so it is left untranslated as cited. 'ii lib.' read as book ii.

passages.original: In templis isdem pro iisdem, dixit Ennius. Hinc Cicero eodem in loco ait isdem dici et in nominativo singulari, et in ablativo plurali, et utrumque usurpa- tum fuisse ab Ennio : nam vox isdem derivatur ab is, ea, id, et demum, auctore Prisciano lib. xii, cap. de figura. Hinc, si non isdem, sed idem, campus le- geretur, ut nunc p(??)ofecto legitur, sed corrupte qui- dem Ciceronis de hac voce disputatio vana esset. Ennius enim quamvis in nominativo ing(??)lari dixerit, isdem, non idem campus, in ablativo plurali etiam dixit in templis isdem, pro iisdem, et uti malu(??)t ea- dem voce in secundo loco, alterum i, abjiciens nt malum sonum vitaret, quae pro iisdem, vocem eis- dem usurparet, quae sane vox (ut ait Cicero) erat opimior, quam scilicet ferebat Ennii aetas, quae ni- mirum vetustatem sapiebat.
passages.english: Ennius said "in templis isdem" for iisdem. Hence Cicero says in the same place that isdem is used both in the nominative singular and in the ablative plural, and that both were used by Ennius; for the word isdem is derived from is, ea, id and demum, on the authority of Priscian, book xii, in the chapter on form. Hence, if the reading were not isdem but idem campus, as it is certainly read now, though corruptly, Cicero's discussion of this word would be pointless. For although Ennius said isdem campus, not idem, in the nominative singular, he also said in templis isdem in the ablative plural, for iisdem, and in the second place he preferred to use the same word, dropping the second i to avoid an unpleasant sound, rather than use the word eisdem for iisdem; this word, as Cicero says, was indeed richer, as the age of Ennius evidently permitted, an age which no doubt had a flavour of antiquity.
passages.notes: Scanning errors read as 'profecto', 'singulari', 'maluit', 'ut'. The clause 'quae pro iisdem, vocem eisdem usurparet' is awkward (probably for 'quam ... '); translated as 'rather than use eisdem'. 'Opimior' (richer, fuller) as applied to the word is Cicero's term; its exact reference is unclear.
